title: Asawsunce
summary: A Brookhaven wetland placename where a Native personal name appears to remain attached to swamp and Yaphank Creek geography.
address_label: Yaphank Creek wetlands south of Yaphank, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern wetland point along Yaphank Creek south of Yaphank; not an exact swamp boundary.
why_this_matters: Asawsunce appears to preserve a Native personal name connected with a swamp and Yaphank Creek locality in Brookhaven. Instead of only describing a landform, the name points toward a person or family remembered through place, showing how Native lives could become embedded in local geography. Wetlands and creek names can hold community memory, not empty space on a map.
introduction_content: Asawsunce is a swamp and Yaphank Creek locality south of the village of Yaphank in Brookhaven. Later forms Oosunk and Oosence belong with this same place rather than separate map records.
translation_content:
Asawsunce is treated as a personal name rather than a descriptive translation. Later forms include Oosunk and Oosence. Those forms should be kept with the same source record rather than mapped as separate places.

Why Place Names Matter

“The use of Aboriginal place names and languages recognises the deep histories of specific places for Aboriginal peoples; enables broader understanding of Aboriginal culture and the significance of places; and provides a pathway for truth telling, healing and reconciliation.”

— Northern Territory Place Names Committee, Aboriginal Place Names and Dual Naming Policy (2025), The use of Aboriginal place names and languages section
whereintheworld_content: Asawsunce preserves a named wetland and a remembered Native presence along Yaphank Creek. The history also shows how personal names and wetland boundaries became part of colonial land records.
